in_vehicle.rule: If a person and a vehicle (car, suv, truck, van, bus or any of their words) appear with 'in', 'inside', 'into', 'driving', 'drives', 'driver', 'behind the wheel', 'passenger', 'back seat', or a sit verb right before the vehicle ('sitting a car', missing 'in'), SEAT the person with seatInVehicle(person, vehicle, seat, pose) instead of placing them beside the vehicle. 'next to', 'beside', 'by', 'near', 'outside', 'leaning on', 'against', 'on the hood' and 'behind the <vehicle>' keep the person outside. 'driver' / 'driving' with no vehicle word adds a car. A child alone in a vehicle goes to the back seat. 'on the bus' seats a bus passenger.
in_vehicle.parser: assets/in_vehicle_parse.js: parseInVehicle(text) -> { vehicle, people: [{ seat, pose, preset }] } or null
in_vehicle.helper: assets/in_vehicle.js: seatInVehicle(person, vehicle, seat = 'driver', pose = null) (also exported from assets/index.js)

person.crowd_note: createPerson({ preset: 'crowd' }): same joints, attach points and look at mannequin detail 0.1; kit items take options.preset = 'crowd'

subject_swap.rule: buildKit(layout, { subject: { pose, props } }) drops every kit item whose subjectSwap equals the subject's pose id or one of its prop asset ids (props as an array or a slot map); the dropped ids are in root.userData.dropped. Use it when the prompt subject brings its own ball (kick, throw, catch) so the kit ball does not double up.
